help.dashboard:
“Key metrics” — a summary of your business for the selected period: revenue, clients, visits, and staff occupancy.

Only appointments marked “Client arrived” count. An appointment without a client phone number doesn't add to the client count.

The percentage next to each tile compares against the previous period of the same length.
help.visits: “Visits” is a working list of upcoming and recent appointments: confirm an appointment with the checkmark, see the full edit history in the activity feed on the right.

tiles.total: Money received: visit payments minus refunds, plus paid products. Below — the number of operations: services performed and product units sold
tiles.services: Visit payments received (a transfer prepayment counts once) minus client refunds. Below — services performed, including discounted and membership ones
tiles.products: Paid product sales — during a visit and without one. Payments from the client account are not included
tiles.avgVisit: (Service revenue + product revenue) ÷ number of receipts. A receipt is a visit (several bookings of one client on one day = one visit) or a standalone product sale
tiles.avgService: Service revenue ÷ number of services provided
tiles.avgProduct: Product revenue ÷ number of product sales
tiles.clients: Unique clients who visited in the period — each person counted once
tiles.visits: “Client arrived” visits: several bookings of one client on one day are one visit; a client is counted once per visit
tiles.appointments: All bookings in the period by visit date, including cancelled and deleted ones
tiles.newClients: First visit to the salon ever within the selected period (in Retention, “new” means new to a given master, so it is higher there)
tiles.returningClients: First visit was before the period, but they came back within it
tiles.lostClients: Haven't visited for longer than the churn period setting
tiles.completed: Bookings marked “Client arrived”. There can be more bookings than visits: a visit is all of a client’s bookings on one day
tiles.cancelled: Bookings cancelled by the client or the salon, and deleted ones
tiles.avgOccupancy: Total duration of “arrived” appointments ÷ total duration of staff shifts in the period
tiles.rebooking: Of the clients who came in the period — how many already have a next booking after their last visit
tiles.revenuePerHour: Sales (services + products) ÷ scheduled master shift hours in the period

help.retention: “Client retention” — for each staff member: how many clients they had, how many were new and how many returned. “Retention, %” is computed over a recent window (the churn period) — it shows truly loyal clients of that staff member, unlike “Returning”, which counts any past visit with no time limit. Here “New” means the client hadn't visited THIS STAFF MEMBER before (not the salon overall, as on the Dashboard); “Clients in the prior window” are those who visited them in an equal-length period right before the current one.
help.workload: “Staff workload” — how much of the scheduled time a staff member actually worked, how much was idle, and how many bookings they have ahead. Occupancy only counts completed visits (“Client arrived”).
help.events: “Events” — all group bookings for the period with fill rate and payments. A cancelled event stays in the report — its row turns red instead of disappearing.
help.financeReport: “Financial report” — income and expenses for the period by item, day and register. Built from financial operations; cancelled operations are excluded.
help.pnl: “P&L report” — profit and loss over 12 months. “Total before tax” = revenue minus expenses. Click any amount to see the operations behind it.
help.cashDay: “Daily cash report” — end-of-day register reconciliation: how much came in, what's in each register, and the full feed of the day's operations.
help.salesByStaff: “By staff” — how much each staff member brought in and how: services or products. Cost per hour = revenue ÷ hours worked.
help.salesByStaffDynamics: “By staff over time” — the selected staff member's numbers by month, starting from a chosen month.
help.salesByServices: “By services” — demand and money for each service. Profit = paid in money minus consumables cost (from the tech card) minus the staff member's payroll for that service. “Upsold” shows how many times and for how much the service was added to a visit as an add-on.
help.salesByClients: “By clients” — who brought in how much: revenue, share, average receipt and visit count for the period.
help.dataExports: “Data operations” — a log of every export and import: who, when and what. The owner sees exports made by every staff member.
help.stockBalance: “Inventory balance” shows what's in stock right now (or on any past date), its cost and markup, and the total value tied up in it.
help.stockOrders: “Product orders” lists everything below its desired stock level with the shortage to reorder.
help.stockSalesAnalysis: “Product sales analysis” shows what sells, how much, and at what markup.
help.stockUsageAnalysis: “Consumable usage analysis” compares actual consumable write-offs against the treatment-card norm.
help.stockWriteOffAnalysis: “Product write-off analysis” shows stock movement for the period: opening balance, income, outflow, closing balance.
help.stockTurnover: “Inventory turnover” shows how fast stock sells and how many days of stock remain.
help.promotions: “Promotions” shows whether a promotion brings new clients and whether they come back, plus the revenue and staff involved.
help.reviews: “Reviews” shows client reviews of the business and stars given to staff for the selected period.
help.messages: “Messages” is a log of everything sent to clients, staff and admins — type, channel, status and text.
help.calls: “Call logs” shows call history and recordings once IP telephony is connected.
help.dataChanges: “Data changes” shows who created, edited or deleted a booking, financial or stock operation.
help.appointments: Every booking in the period: any source, any status, including soft-deleted ones. Filter by created date, visit date, staff, status, cancelled, source and services, then press Show. "Excel operations" exports the found rows (up to 5000) or imports old bookings from a file.

archive.title: Archive, merge, delete — what stays in reports

product.effect: disappears from the list, but report statistics stay; payroll drops it from calculation

membershipType.effect: analytics, statistics and history stay unchanged

mergeServices.effect: irreversible: history, analytics and finance operations get rewritten under the new service

deleteService.effect: irreversible, loses related operations and settings; already-deleted rows in "Bookings" keep showing its old name

deleteProduct.effect: irreversible: past stock reports lose its rows

deleteCardType.effect: cascades to delete every issued card of that type

staffFired.effect: firing keeps statistics; deleting erases their data, but their bookings stay in "Bookings"
